title: Chapter 250: He Was Going on a Date
html:
It does feel safer with the hammer.

Chen Ge shouldered his backpack and left the Haunted House, phone in hand. Lychee had begun her third story. Its details were so vivid that she might have experienced them herself.

Most disturbing of all, it appeared to continue the first tale. The taxi driver in this story was the ghost created at the end of that one.

A ghost taxi driver, that does sound like their style.

Chen Ge waited a long time outside New Century Park before finally finding a taxi. It was already 11:30 p.m.

Should be enough time.

When Chen Ge opened the door, an old-fashioned song drifted from the radio. The air conditioner was off. A middle-aged driver rested one arm on the window and nodded to the rhythm.

This man looks so familiar.

After studying the man’s face, he finally remembered. This driver had taken him to Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy for Zhang Ya’s Bloody Heart Mission. When a knife accidentally slipped from Chen Ge’s pocket as he reached for his phone, the driver had assumed he was being robbed and used the illuminated roof sign to call for help. Their meeting again was an extraordinary coincidence.

“Where are you going?”

Afraid the driver might refuse him if recognized, Chen Ge covered half his face and quickly climbed inside. He shut the door. “Huai Hua Street in the old quarter. I’m in a hurry, so please drive quickly.”

“Huai Hua Street?” The driver lowered the volume on his radio. It seemed like he was conflicted.

“Is there a problem? Do you need extra money?”

“It isn’t far, but people say the street is cursed. Many drivers refuse to go there.”

“You still believe in stuff like that in this day and age?” Chen Ge said without batting an eye. “Do you mind hurrying? I’m in a rush.”

“Sometimes you have no choice but to believe. A few weeks ago, something strange happened to me.” The driver started the engine. “A man asked me to take him to an abandoned school in the middle of the night. I thought nothing of it and drove him there. Can you guess what happened?”

“What?”

“He said he was going there for a date. Can you imagine how I felt? I was alone at midnight with a madman in my car. I feared for my life!” The more the driver spoke, the more agitated he became. “I developed a fever the next day. It truly was a curse. I sent my wife to obtain a talisman from a nearby temple, and only after resting for a week did I find the courage to drive again.”

“Was it that scary?” Chen Ge felt embarrassed. He did not realize that his adventures would cause trouble for others.

“You have to believe me. I’m not lying. The man was about your size. He looked perfectly normal, but who knows...” The driver glanced at Chen Ge in the rearview mirror, and a chill crept upward from his feet. Why does he look so familiar?

The color on his face faded, and he asked as a test, “Brother, have we met somewhere before?”

Certain the man had recognized him, Chen Ge confessed. “Thank you for driving me to Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy that night. I’m sorry—I didn’t realize the experience had troubled you so much.”

The driver’s face froze. He took out the talisman from inside his clothes and tore it up. “Actually, I recognized you when you got in the car. I was just kidding, I hope you don’t mind.”

“Of course not. What should I call you? I work at the amusement park; perhaps we can be friends.” This was their second chance encounter. Whatever the driver thought of him, Chen Ge admired the man’s optimism.

The driver looked at the completely empty and dark amusement park, and he said in a quivering voice, “My name is Zhang.”

They spoke for a while, but the driver remained guarded, like a rabbit trapped in a cage with a lion. Veins stood out on the hands gripping the wheel.

The sight left Chen Ge helpless. He had clearly traumatized the driver that night. Since the man showed no desire for friendship, Chen Ge stopped pressing and returned his attention to Lychee’s program, hoping for clues about the Ghost Stories Society.

Eerie music filled the car as Lychee continued telling stories set on Huai Hua Street, each involving a taxi driver as the victim. Sweat beaded on Uncle Zhang’s forehead. He tried not to listen and concentrated on the road.

With nineteen minutes remaining until midnight, the taxi reached the old quarter. Uncle Zhang stopped roughly fifty meters from Huai Hua Street and refused to advance, no matter what Chen Ge said. Feeling sorry for him, Chen Ge paid and left without argument.

The moment he closed the door, the taxi drove away without hesitation.

Am I that scary? The uncle sure is a coward.

Chen Ge watched the taxi depart, only for it to stop another fifty meters down the road. Someone in a nearby alley was hailing it.

A shadow emerged from the alley and entered the car. Eager to leave the area, Uncle Zhang sped away the moment the door closed.

Wait, someone was calling for a taxi?

Chen Ge replayed the stranger’s movements in his mind. Distance and darkness had obscured the figure’s appearance.

Wait, the person who exited the alley…

Chen Ge narrowed his eyes.

They were running backwards!

Chen Ge pocketed his phone. Lychee had begun her fifth taxi-driver story. He ran toward the alley, but the car was already gone.

I need to find him!Chen Ge rushed to stand in the middle of the street. He did not care whether the next taxi had passengers in it or not; he halted it.

“There should be a chat group among all the taxi drivers, right? Help me find someone, quick! He’s in mortal danger!”

The driver recoiled from Chen Ge, but after hearing his description, managed to contact Uncle Zhang.

“Uncle Zhang, where are you now?”

“Every passenger tonight is strange. I just dropped someone at Huai Hua Street, and now this customer wants to visit the bus stop beside Jiujiang Crematorium. Says he left something there.”
